In this lesson you will be troubleshooting various faults in a FDM transmitter and receiver system.
INTRODUCTIONM
Troubleshooting an FDM system is no different than troubleshooting the other signal processing systems. You have learned, only the signals and components are different.
If you recall, FDM systems are comprised of FM modulators and demodulators. This makes troubleshooting an FDM system easy since you have previously worked with FM circuits.

PC130-324 SCHEMATIC - Transmitter
The transmitter consists of the components necessary to frequency multiplex information signals.
Definition
The receiver consists of the components necessary to demultiplex FDM signals.
To locate a faulted chip or support component, you must first determine if the FDM system is operating correctly.
To do this, you check each input signal to the transmitter against each output signal of the receiver.
If one or more of the output signals are incorrect, then the system is faulted.
If the system is faulted, you determine if the transmitter or receiver is causing the problem.
If the output of the transmitter is bad, the multiplexer circuits are faulted.
If the output of the transmitter is good, the fault is in the transmission medium or receiver.
If the input to the receiver is bad, the fault is in the transmission medium.
If the input to the receiver is good, the demultiplexer circuits are faulted.
